briefing.title: Not a pile of tools — one chain from theory to evidence
briefing.lead: Every section is its own page: jump straight to a workspace from the nav, stay on one topic, no hunting inside an endless scroll.

p1.label: 01 / Concept
p1.title: First, build the language
p1.text: One consistent set of symbols, assumptions and derivations ties CAPM, the SDF, Black–Scholes and OLS into a single language instead of scattered formulas.

p2.label: 02 / Experiment
p2.title: Then run the experiment
p2.text: Parameters, data and stress scenarios live in one interface, so you can watch outputs move with assumptions and spot the sensitive variables fast.

p3.label: 03 / Research
p3.title: Finally, keep the output
p3.text: Notebooks, templates, a paper index and reusable charts turn lectures, strategy prototypes and empirical homework into reproducible workflows.

learning.intro: A continuous ladder from mathematical foundations to economic intuition, pricing theory and empirical research. Each stage links straight to the lab pages that teach it.

prob.title: Probability, statistics & econometric method
prob.desc: Random variables, distributions, LLN/CLT, then OLS, MLE, IV and GMM — the identification assumptions everything else rests on.

micro.title: Micro & macro foundations
micro.desc: Preferences, constraints, equilibrium and strategic interaction; then growth, business cycles and policy rules at the aggregate level.

fin.title: Pricing fundamentals
fin.desc: No-arbitrage, risk-neutral valuation, Black–Scholes and the implied-volatility surface — the shared language of financial models.

ap.title: Asset pricing & portfolio choice
ap.desc: From the stochastic discount factor and CAPM-family models to factor construction, mean–variance optimisation and the efficient frontier.

risk.title: Risk measurement & fixed income
risk.desc: VaR, expected shortfall, backtesting and capital rules; curve construction, duration and structured cash flows.

adv.title: Quant research & reproducible output
adv.desc: Signal construction, the Qlib pipeline, out-of-sample evaluation and backtests you can hand over as a research artefact.

topics.intro: Every topic follows the same three-part structure — core question, key models, empirical application — so it works both as a revision outline and as an entry point for your own research.
